name: LT3652IMSE#TRPBF
title: Power tracking 2 A step-down battery charger for solar power
summary: The LT3652 is a 1 MHz non-synchronous buck charger with an integrated 2 A switch, running from 4.95 V to 32 V (40 V absolute maximum). It charges with constant current then constant voltage; the float voltage is set by a divider onto a 3.3 V feedback reference, up to 14.4 V, so it serves Li-ion/polymer, LiFePO4 and sealed lead-acid batteries. An input-voltage regulation loop cuts charge current whenever the input drops below a programmed level, holding a solar panel at its peak-power voltage. Charging ends at C/10 or on a capacitor-set timer, and two open-collector pins report status.
key_figures: 4.95 V to 32 V (40 V absolute maximum)
up to 2 A, set by RSENSE
up to 14.4 V, from a 3.3 V reference (0.5 %)
12-lead 3 mm × 3 mm DFN (DD), 12-lead MSOP with exposed pad (MSE)

notes: The E and I grades differ in the temperature range over which the electrical figures are guaranteed (Note 2 of the electrical characteristics). Some packages also come on 500-unit reels with a #TRMPBF suffix.

pins.name: VIN
pins.function: Supply input for the charger, 4.95 V to 32 V. For a dependable start it must sit 3.3 V above the programmed float voltage; once BOOST is at least 2 V above SW it runs down to VBAT(FLT) + 0.75 V. Draws about 85 µA after termination.

pins.name: VIN_REG
pins.function: Input regulation reference. Under 2.7 V the charger lowers its current limit, so a divider from VIN sets the lowest VIN the charger will pull the supply to, such as a panel's peak-power voltage. Tie to VIN when unused.

pins.name: SHDN
pins.function: Precise shutdown input: enables at 1.2 V rising with 120 mV hysteresis, so a divider can make it an undervoltage lockout. Below 0.4 V the part enters low-current shutdown (15 µA from VIN). Bias current is about 10 nA. Tie to VIN when unused.

pins.name: CHRG
pins.function: Charge status. Pulled low while the charge current is above C/10 and during a temperature fault; high impedance after C/10 termination, or when the timer is in use and current has fallen under C/10. Sinks up to 10 mA; may be pulled up as high as VIN.

pins.name: FAULT
pins.function: Fault status. Pulled low for a battery temperature fault and, when the timer is used, for a bad-battery fault; high impedance otherwise. Sinks up to 10 mA; may be pulled up as high as VIN.

pins.name: TIMER
pins.function: End-of-cycle timer. A capacitor to ground sets the full-charge time (0.68 µF gives 3 hours and a 22.5 minute precondition limit). Grounding the pin disables the timer and charging ends at C/10.

pins.name: VFB
pins.function: Float voltage feedback. Charging regulates this pin to 3.3 V through a divider from BAT; a new cycle starts when it falls 2.5 % below. Bias current is 110 nA, cancelled by a 250k equivalent divider resistance.

pins.name: NTC
pins.function: Battery thermistor input. Sources 50 µA into a 10 kΩ, B = 3380 NTC to ground. Above 1.36 V (below 0 °C) or below 0.29 V (above 40 °C) charging pauses and both status pins go low; each threshold has about 5 °C hysteresis. Stays enabled while the resistance to ground is under 250k; leave open to disable.

pins.name: BAT
pins.function: Charger output monitor and the reference end of the current-sense resistor. Needs 10 µF to ground. Draws under 0.1 µA once charging has ended.

pins.name: SENSE
pins.function: Current-sense input: RSENSE sits between SENSE and BAT, and 100 mV across it is the maximum charge current. Draws under 0.1 µA once charging has ended.

pins.name: BOOST
pins.function: Bootstrap supply for the switch driver. A capacitor of 1 µF or more goes to SW; a diode from the battery or another source refreshes it. Operating range 0 V to 8.5 V above SW.

pins.name: SW
pins.function: Switch output, the emitter of the internal power switch, which connects SW to VIN when on. Effective on-resistance with the boosted drive is 0.175 Ω.

pins.name: GND
pins.function: Ground and exposed thermal pad on the underside; solder it to the board ground plane.

circuits.title: 2 A solar panel power manager with 7.2 V LiFePO4 battery and 17 V peak power tracking
circuits.description: A solar panel feeds VIN through D1. R1/R2 hold VIN_REG at 2.7 V when the panel is at about 17 V, so the charger backs off its current rather than dragging the panel below its peak-power point. SHDN is tied to VIN, TIMER is grounded for C/10 termination, and the status pins are unused. The buck stage is SW, the 10 µH inductor, the 0.05 Ω sense resistor (2 A) and freewheel diode D2; C2 and D3 from BAT make the bootstrap supply. R4/R5 set the float voltage for a two-cell LiFePO4 pack, and the pack's 10k thermistor watches its temperature. The system load sits on the input rail, and D4 runs from BAT (anode) to that rail (cathode).

parts.note: NTC thermistor, B = 3380, in the battery pack

parts.value: Solar panel input (<40 V open circuit)

circuits.title: 2-cell Li-ion charger (8.3 V at 2 A) with 3 hour timer termination from a 12 V, 1 A unregulated wall adapter
circuits.description: An unregulated 12 V, 1 A adapter feeds VIN through D1. The chain R1, R2, R3 from the adapter sets VIN_REG at its R1/R2 junction so the charger trims its current to keep the adapter from sagging below 12 V, and sets SHDN at the R2/R3 junction. C4 (0.68 µF) on TIMER gives a three-hour end of cycle. LED1 and LED2 with 10k resistors show CHRG and FAULT. The buck stage uses the Vishay 8.2 µH inductor, the 0.05 Ω sense resistor for 2 A, and freewheel diode D3; D2 (1N914) from BAT refreshes the bootstrap capacitor C2. R7/R8 set an 8.3 V float for the removable two-cell pack, whose 10k thermistor goes to NTC. C5 and C6 hold the output up for the system load when the pack is out.

parts.note: NTC thermistor R1, B = 3380, in the pack

circuits.title: Basic 2 A 1-cell LiFePO4 charger (3.6 V float) with C/10 termination
circuits.description: A minimal charger for one LiFePO4 cell from 5 V to 32 V. VIN_REG and SHDN are tied to VIN, so neither input regulation nor shutdown is used; TIMER is grounded for C/10 termination and NTC, CHRG and FAULT are left open. The buck stage is SW, 5.6 µH, the 0.05 Ω sense resistor for 2 A and freewheel diode D1; D2 (CMDSH2-4L) from BAT refreshes the bootstrap capacitor C2. The float voltage comes from the three-resistor network R2 (30k), R3 (330k) and R4 (223k), which gives 3.6 V with a 250k source resistance at VFB.

parts.value: VIN, 5 V to 32 V (40 V max)

circuits.title: 1 A solar panel powered 3-stage 12 V lead-acid fast/float charger
circuits.description: A panel with a 16 V peak-power point feeds VIN through D1; R1/R2 hold VIN_REG at 2.7 V at that voltage, and SHDN is tied to VIN. The 0.1 Ω sense resistor sets 1 A, with 0.15 A trickle charge below 10 V. TIMER has 4.7 µF to ground for timer termination. The float divider R5 (309k) over R6 (100k) through R4 (174k) gives 13.5 V; while CHRG is low (charging above C/10) it pulls the divider's lower node down through R7 (1M) and D4, raising the target to 14.4 V, so the charger fast-charges to 14.4 V, drops to a 13.5 V float once current falls to 0.1 A, and restarts fast charge below 13.2 V. The Murata 10k thermistor with R3 (910 Ω) in series moves the hot limit to 45 °C, for a 0 °C to 45 °C window. The bootstrap supply comes from BAT through zener Z1 (BZX84C6V2L) and D2 (1N914) to keep BOOST within its range at a 14.4 V battery. Inductor is a Würth 22 µH; D3 freewheels.

parts.value: Solar panel input (<40 V open circuit, 16 V peak power)

operation.text: A 1 MHz fixed-frequency, average-current-mode buck. The voltage error amplifier compares VFB with the 3.3 V reference and drives ITH; ITH divided by ten is the current command to a current error amplifier that compares it with the RSENSE voltage, and that amplifier's output sets the switch duty against a ramp. ITH is clamped at 1 V, which caps the sense voltage at 100 mV and so sets the constant-current level. ITH is pulled down when VIN_REG goes under 2.7 V or the die nears 125 °C.

Below VFB = 2.3 V (70 % of float) the charger preconditions at 15 % of full current (15 mV across RSENSE), with 70 mV of hysteresis. Above it the charger runs at full current until VFB nears 3.3 V, then holds constant voltage while current tapers. C/10 is detected when ITH reaches 0.1 V (10 mV across RSENSE).

Selected by grounding TIMER. The cycle ends when current falls under one tenth of the programmed maximum; the part goes to standby and CHRG goes high impedance. There is no bad-battery detection in this mode. With the battery removed the output saws by about 100 mV between termination and recharge, which makes an LED on CHRG blink at a rate set by the output capacitance.

Selected by a capacitor on TIMER. CHRG still drops out at C/10, but charging carries on topping off until the end-of-cycle time (3 hours with 0.68 µF). The cycle only ends if the battery reached at least 97.5 % of float; otherwise the timer restarts for another full cycle.

With the timer in use, a battery that stays below the precondition threshold longer than 1/8 of the cycle, or drops back into precondition after that point, is a bad-battery fault: charging stops, CHRG goes high impedance and FAULT goes low. The charger then sources 0.5 mA, so pulling the bad battery lets the output rise and a new cycle starts when another battery is fitted; cycling power or SHDN also restarts it.

After termination the internal float reference drops 2.5 %, the voltage error amplifier output falls under 0.3 V and the part goes to standby, drawing 85 µA from VIN. When the battery sags below 97.5 % of float the amplifier output rises again and a new cycle starts.

If the source cannot supply the charger its voltage falls. A divider from the source to VIN_REG makes the desired minimum correspond to 2.7 V; the charger lowers its current to keep VIN_REG at or above that, which for a solar panel holds it near the peak-power voltage. Tie VIN_REG to VIN when unused.

A crystalline panel's open-circuit voltage falls by roughly 2 mV/°C per cell, and its peak-power voltage follows nearly the same slope. An LM234 temperature sensor in the VIN_REG divider makes the regulation point follow that linear drift.

The buck is non-synchronous, so with no bootstrap voltage the switch needs VIN – VSW ≥ 3.3 V; while idle SW sits at the battery voltage, so VIN has to be 3.3 V above VBAT(FLT) to start. Once the BOOST capacitor holds more than 2 V the requirement goes away. BOOST takes a 1 µF or larger capacitor to SW, refreshed by a diode rated above 0.1 A average and above VIN(MAX) reverse, from the battery or another source; for floats above 8.4 V a >100 mA zener in series keeps BOOST within its 8.5 V range. An outside BOOST supply removes the start-up requirement at low VIN.
SHDN has a precise 1.2 V threshold so a divider can serve as undervoltage lockout. Pulled under 0.4 V the part draws 15 µA from VIN.

A 10 kΩ, B = 3380 thermistor near the pack, from NTC to ground, sees 50 µA. Outside 0.29 V to 1.36 V (above 40 °C or below 0 °C) charging is paused, both status pins go low and the timer holds. Each threshold has about 5 °C of hysteresis. A 0.91k resistor in series with the thermistor raises the hot limit to 45 °C. Leave NTC open to disable.
The current limit is cut back as the junction nears 125 °C, usually by only a little. If it falls under C/10 with TIMER grounded, the part suspends charging in standby until it cools.
VIN carries large switched currents and needs a low-ESR capacitor rated for the input ripple current; half of ICHG(MAX) is the worst case used for design.

BAT needs a 10 µF ceramic in every design. To run a system load with the battery removed, or with long battery leads, add 100 µF of low-ESR non-ceramic capacitance (tantalum or polymer) in parallel; otherwise ripple or oscillation can appear. The capacitor voltage rating must be at least the float voltage.
The SW-to-ground diode must be a Schottky rated above the maximum VIN in reverse; lower forward drop means lower loss.

VFB is high impedance: keep stray capacitance and coupled signals off it. A 20 pF to 50 pF feedforward capacitor from BAT to VFB reduces the effect of parasitics. Board contamination shifts the output voltage, so clean after assembly and use low-leakage flux.

Lead-acid float voltage falls about 3.3 mV/°C per cell (2.25 V per cell at 25 °C). An LM234 in the float divider gives a linear slope; a thermistor network in the divider can approach the slightly curved ideal over a working range.

SW edges are under 10 ns: keep the SW trace short and place CIN and the BOOST capacitor close to the IC with short, wide traces. Route SENSE and BAT together and keep them and VFB short, shielded by a ground plane. Keep high switched currents away from battery ground: in the on state the loop runs CIN, switch, inductor, battery; in the off state it runs from ground via the freewheel diode; in both, the return is via CBAT. Solder the exposed pad to as large a copper area as possible.
